prompt: What is HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World)?

options.text: A multi-layer graph of proximity graphs; search starts in the sparse upper layer and descends, scaling roughly logarithmically.
A clustering method that assigns vectors to Voronoi cells and probes the closest cells.
A compression method that splits vectors into sub-vectors and quantizes each.
A keyword index based on term frequency and inverse document frequency.

explanation: Malkov and Yashunin describe HNSW as an incrementally built multi-layer structure of proximity graphs. Each element's maximum layer is drawn from an exponentially decaying distribution, and starting at the top layer allows logarithmic complexity scaling. Option b describes IVF, c product quantization and d BM25 foundations.

sources.title: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using HNSW graphs (Malkov & Yashunin)
